comments.content: The race guard is only applied to the success path; the sibling .catch still writes to #detail-kv unconditionally, so the very race this fix targets remains reachable via a late-rejecting stale fetch. Scenario: open run A (fetch A stalls) → click run B → fetch B resolves and renderDetail(B) fills #detail-kv → fetch A then rejects (conn reset / 504 / 404 after cleanup) → the catch overwrites B's rendered key-values with "找不到该运行的记录…" while selected === B. The view shows a wrong "not found" error for the currently selected run until the 30s refreshDetail interval re-renders (line 842). Apply the same guard in the catch.
comments.thinking: Now I have a full picture: - `route()` sets `selected = id` synchronously, aborts previous live streams, clears poll timer. - The new guard in `.then` correctly checks `selected !== id`. - `followLive` and `refreshDetail` already have their own `selected === id` guards. - The `.catch` in `route()` (line 834) does NOT have a guard — it writes the "not found" message into `#detail-kv` unconditionally. Failure scenario for the unguarded catch: 1. User opens run A's detail (hash `#A`). `selected = "A"`; fetch A is in flight and stalls/fails slowly (e.g., connection reset after B loads, or a 504 that takes tens of seconds). 2. User clicks run B in the list (hash `#B`). `route()` runs: `selected = "B"`; fetch B starts. 3. Fetch B resolves → guard passes → `renderDetail(B)` fills `#detail-kv` with B's data; `followLive(B)` starts. 4. Fetch A then rejects → `.catch` fires unconditionally → `#detail-kv` innerHTML is replaced with the "找不到该运行的记录（可能已被 30 天清理）" message. Result: the user is looking at run B (live stream running for B), but the detail panel shows a "record not found" error belonging to run A. This is exactly the failure class the commit claims to fix ("晚到的旧 run 不得覆盖当前选中"), but only the success path was guarded — the failure path of the same race remains. Self-healing is at most 30s later via the `refreshDetail` interval (line 842), but only after up to 30 seconds of corrupted UI; and refreshDetail's catch returns false without re-rendering, but on success it would re-render. Actually wait — refreshDetail(B) at next 30s tick would succeed and re-render, so corruption lasts up to 30s. Still a genuine correctness defect on a real path. Is this within review scope? The catch line is unchanged context in the diff. But the review's mandate is the fix commit for the race guard; the incomplete guard is a defect of the change (the change's stated purpose is not fully achieved). The instructions say "Avoid commenting on ... unchanged code" — however this is a case where the changed code's fix is incomplete, and the comment can be anchored to the newly added guard lines... Actually the code_comment tool requires `existing_code` to be newly added lines. I can anchor on the guard block and mention the catch asymmetry, suggesting to guard the catch too. Hmm, but is the catch race "must fix" per user's severity boundary? "不改就会出错的问题——正确性缺陷" — yes: wrong UI state shown to user for the currently selected run, triggered by realistic timing (network slowness + navigation). The comment must give a concrete failure scenario, which I have. But wait — let me also double check whether there's any other issue in the new code itself: 1. Guard placement is correct — `selected = id` is set synchronously before fetch, and `route()` is the only place changing `selected` (lines 818, 824), plus nothing else. So `selected !== id` correctly detects navigation away. 2. Early return in `.then` — fine. 3. Comment quality — the rules say don't report comment/naming issues. Fine. 4. `renderDetail(run)` — run guaranteed object since fetchJSON rejects non-ok and parses JSON. Fine. 5. One more consideration: when the guard returns early (stale response), nothing renders — correct, since the newer route() will handle rendering. But what if the newer route's fetch is still pending? Then detail-kv shows stale/empty until it resolves — acceptable. 6. Another edge: user selects A, fetch A slow; user goes back to list (`selected = null`); fetch A resolves → guard returns → fine. If fetch A rejects → catch writes error into hidden detail-kv — invisible, harmless, and gets overwritten next time a run is opened (route shows detail-view; then fetch resolves and renderDetail replaces detail-kv). Edge: fetch for the new run fails too — error message correct. OK. So the only reportable issue: the `.catch` lacks the same guard, letting a late-rejecting stale fetch overwrite the current selection's detail. Severity: medium? The user's boundary demands correctness defects. The visible corruption window is up to 30s (until refreshDetail interval re-renders), and the scenario requires the old fetch to reject after the new one resolves. Also note: refreshDetail on the 30s interval only re-renders on fetch success; if B's fetch works (which it did in step 3), then B refresh works, so corruption heals in ≤30s. Still wrong behavior meanwhile. Also there's another subtle path: `markStageBoundary` → `refreshDetail` could also heal sooner. Severity: I'd say "medium" — transient UI corruption, self-healing ≤30s, but definitely a correctness defect in exactly the class being fixed. Given the round-2 P2 was about this race, this is an incomplete fix of a P2. I'll report as bug, medium severity (maybe high? The boundary says only must-fix; medium severity fits "correctness defect with limited blast radius"). I'll go with medium. Suggestion: add the same guard to catch: ```js .catch(() => { if (selected !== id) return; $("detail-kv").innerHTML = '找不到该运行的记录（可能已被 30 天清理）。'; }); ``` Anchor: the newly added lines (guard block) — but the comment targets the catch. The tool requires existing_code to be in the diff's added lines. The added lines are: ``` .then((run) => { // 慢响应竞态守卫：晚到的旧 run 不得覆盖当前选中，也不得抢占实时流。 if (selected !== id) return; renderDetail(run); followLive(id); }) ``` I'll anchor on that block and explain the catch asymmetry. The suggestion_code should include the full corrected .then/.catch block to show where the guard goes. Wait, one more check: is there any other new issue? What about `followLive` being skipped when guard returns — if the user navigated A→B, route() for B already set up its own follow. Fine. What about the scenario where fetch A resolves while `selected === null` (list view) — guard returns, no followLive — correct. Also check: `route()` is triggered by hashchange; rapid double navigation A→B→A: route(A1) fetch pending; route(B) fetch; route(A2) fetch. Guard checks `selected !== id` — but A1 and A2 have the same id! If A1 (stale, from first visit) resolves after A2's route, `selected === id === A`, so guard passes and renders — but that's fine, it's the same run's data; worst case slightly older snapshot, then followLive(A) called again — followLive aborts previous (line 735) — fine. No bug. One more: does the guard need `liveAbort` consideration? No. So single comment. Let me also make sure severity mapping: "bug", medium. Content (English per "Always respond in English"?
